questions.q: How does a window function (using OVER) differ from a regular aggregate function used with GROUP BY?
options: A window function always returns fewer columns than GROUP BY
There is no difference — OVER and GROUP BY are interchangeable
A window function computes a value per row over a defined window, without collapsing the individual rows the way GROUP BY does
Window functions can only be used with COUNT, never SUM
questions.explain: OVER() turns an aggregate into a per-row calculation over a window of rows, while GROUP BY collapses rows into one row per group.

questions.q: In `SUM(amount) OVER (PARTITION BY vendor_id ORDER BY check_date)`, what does PARTITION BY do?
options: It deletes rows for other suppliers
It sorts the entire result set by vendor_id
It has no effect unless combined with HAVING
It restarts the running calculation for each distinct vendor_id, similar in spirit to GROUP BY but without collapsing rows
questions.explain: PARTITION BY divides rows into groups for the window calculation, restarting the running total at each new group, while all rows remain in the output.

questions.q: If two invoices tie for the largest invoice_amount within a supplier's partition, how do ROW_NUMBER() and RANK() differ in numbering them?
options: ROW_NUMBER() assigns them different unique numbers; RANK() assigns them the same rank, then skips ahead for the next distinct value
They behave identically in every case
ROW_NUMBER() assigns them the same number; RANK() does not
Neither function can handle ties at all
questions.explain: ROW_NUMBER() always produces unique sequential numbers regardless of ties, while RANK() gives tied rows an identical rank and then skips subsequent rank numbers.

questions.q: What is the key difference between RANK() and DENSE_RANK() when handling tied values?
options: There is no difference between them
DENSE_RANK() does not skip rank numbers after a tie, while RANK() does
RANK() never produces ties; DENSE_RANK() always does
DENSE_RANK() can only be used without PARTITION BY
questions.explain: After a tie, RANK() leaves a gap in the rank sequence, while DENSE_RANK() continues with the very next integer.

questions.q: Which window function would you use to find "the single largest invoice per supplier," keeping exactly one top row per vendor_id?
options: SUM() OVER() with no PARTITION BY
COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY vendor_id)
GROUP BY vendor_id alone, with no window function
ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY vendor_id ORDER BY invoice_amount DESC), then filter where rn = 1
questions.explain: ROW_NUMBER() partitioned by vendor_id and ordered by invoice_amount descending assigns 1 to the largest invoice per supplier, which can then be filtered to.
